# 01 Setup your environment

Run the common setup script and synchronize the local project with
GitHub.

```{r}
# Run the setup script containing package restoration, helper functions, etc.
source(here::here("scripts", "01-setup.R"))

# Pull changes from the online repository into this local project folder.
# This is especially important when collaborating on the same project.
system2("git",c("-C", here::here(), "pull"))

# authenticate your @student.rug.nl google account
gsheets_auth()
```
```{r}
#| label: packages
#| results: hide
lib <- Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_USER")
dir.create(lib, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
.libPaths(c(lib, .libPaths()))
install.packages(lib = lib, dependencies = TRUE)

ipak <- function(pkg){
  new.pkg <- pkg[!(pkg %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])]
  if (length(new.pkg))
    install.packages(new.pkg, dependencies = TRUE)
  sapply(pkg, require, character.only = TRUE)
}

# List of packages needed to run our code. NOTE: tidyverse is loaded LAST, so its
# functions (e.g. dplyr::select, dplyr::filter) win when two packages use the same name.
packages <- c("knitr","rmarkdown","sf","terra","tidyterra","suntools","rnaturalearth",
              "rnaturalearthdata","maptiles","tidyverse")

# sf:                vector data (points, lines, polygons)
# terra:             raster data
# tidyterra:         plot and wrangle terra objects with ggplot2/tidyverse syntax
# suntools:          sunrise, sunset, twilight and solar noon
# rnaturalearth(data): open access spatial data from www.naturalearthdata.com
# maptiles:          download map tiles and satellite imagery (optional step 4.5)
# knitr, rmarkdown:  needed to render this .qmd file to an HTML report
# tidyverse:         readr (reading data), dplyr & tidyr (wrangling), ggplot2 (plotting),
#                    lubridate (dates and times), stringr (text)

ipak(packages)
```

# Download data from Movebank using the move2 package

```{r}
#| label: move2
#| eval: false
library(move2)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

movebank_store_credentials("Zdvnio") #bJd6wHDVZ@_NWVF

lic <- "633902d4cf2f59910c2a9ae96e7d31b2"

# reference data (one row per deployment)
meta <- movebank_download_deployment(study_id = 7431347,
                                     `license-md5` = lic)

# GPS and Argos data together
tracks <- movebank_download_study(study_id       = 7431347,
                                  sensor_type_id = c("gps", "argos-doppler-shift"),
                                  `license-md5`  = lic)

tracks <- tracks %>%
  filter(!st_is_empty(.)) %>%
  mutate(long = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
         lat  = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()

count(tracks, sensor_type_id)

```

# Clean data

```{r}
#| label: subset-zerbst
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(dbscan)
library(maps)

eps_km <- 50   # clustering distance for tagging sites

# ---- Keep untouched originals (so the chunk can be re-run) ------------
if (!exists("meta_raw"))   meta_raw   <- meta
if (!exists("tracks_raw")) tracks_raw <- tracks

# ---- Tagging location per deployment ----------------------------------
xy_from_sfc <- function(x) {
  empty <- st_is_empty(x)
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(x), ncol = 2)
  if (any(!empty)) out[!empty, ] <- st_coordinates(x[!empty])[, 1:2]
  out
}
ok <- function(x, y) !is.na(x) & !is.na(y) & !(x == 0 & y == 0)

on_xy  <- xy_from_sfc(meta_raw$deploy_on_location)
cap_xy <- xy_from_sfc(meta_raw$capture_location)

# First fix per deployment (only a fallback for the tagging location)
first_fix <- tracks_raw |>
  select(deployment_id, sensor_type_id, timestamp, long, lat,
         algorithm_marked_outlier, manually_marked_outlier) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(!is.na(long), !is.na(lat), !is.na(timestamp)) |>
  filter(is.na(algorithm_marked_outlier) | !algorithm_marked_outlier) |>
  filter(is.na(manually_marked_outlier)  | !manually_marked_outlier) |>
  distinct(deployment_id, sensor_type_id, timestamp, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(deployment_id, timestamp) |>
  group_by(deployment_id) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(deployment_id, fix_lon = long, fix_lat = lat)

tag_sites <- tibble(
  deployment_id = meta_raw$deployment_id,
  on_lon  = on_xy[, 1],  on_lat  = on_xy[, 2],
  cap_lon = cap_xy[, 1], cap_lat = cap_xy[, 2]
) |>
  left_join(first_fix, by = "deployment_id") |>
  mutate(
    loc_source = case_when(
      ok(on_lon,  on_lat)  ~ "deploy_on_location",
      ok(cap_lon, cap_lat) ~ "capture_location",
      ok(fix_lon, fix_lat) ~ "first_fix"
    ),
    tag_lon = case_when(loc_source == "deploy_on_location" ~ on_lon,
                        loc_source == "capture_location"   ~ cap_lon,
                        loc_source == "first_fix"          ~ fix_lon),
    tag_lat = case_when(loc_source == "deploy_on_location" ~ on_lat,
                        loc_source == "capture_location"   ~ cap_lat,
                        loc_source == "first_fix"          ~ fix_lat)
  ) |>
  select(deployment_id, loc_source, tag_lon, tag_lat)

# ---- Cluster tagging sites and find the Zerbst cluster -----------------
sites_sf <- tag_sites |>
  filter(!is.na(tag_lon)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("tag_lon", "tag_lat"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

d  <- matrix(as.numeric(st_distance(sites_sf)), nrow = nrow(sites_sf))
cl <- dbscan(as.dist(d), eps = eps_km * 1000, minPts = 1)$cluster

clusters <- sites_sf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(cluster = cl) |>
  group_by(cluster) |>
  summarise(n_deployments = n(),
            clon = mean(tag_lon), clat = mean(tag_lat),
            .groups = "drop")

cent <- st_as_sf(clusters, coords = c("clon", "clat"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

cities <- maps::world.cities |>
  filter(pop >= 10000) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("long", "lat"), crs = 4326)

nearest          <- st_nearest_feature(cent, cities)
clusters$city    <- cities$name[nearest]
clusters$country <- cities$country.etc[nearest]

zerbst_cluster <- clusters |>
  filter(city == "Zerbst", country == "Germany") |>
  pull(cluster)
stopifnot(length(zerbst_cluster) == 1)

zerbst_deployments <- sites_sf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(cluster = cl) |>
  filter(cluster == zerbst_cluster) |>
  pull(deployment_id)

# ---- Exclude individuals with "relocated" in manipulation_type --------
# (all deployments of such an individual are removed)
relocated_individuals <- meta_raw |>
  filter(deployment_id %in% zerbst_deployments,
         str_detect(as.character(manipulation_type), "relocated") %in% TRUE) |>
  pull(individual_id) |>
  unique()

keep_deployments <- meta_raw |>
  filter(deployment_id %in% zerbst_deployments,
         !individual_id %in% relocated_individuals) |>
  pull(deployment_id)

# ---- Create final meta and tracks -------------------------------------
meta   <- meta_raw   |> filter(deployment_id %in% keep_deployments)
tracks <- tracks_raw |> filter(deployment_id %in% keep_deployments)

# Check
tibble(
  zerbst_deployments        = length(zerbst_deployments),
  relocated_individuals_out = length(relocated_individuals),
  deployments_meta          = n_distinct(meta$deployment_id),
  individuals_meta          = n_distinct(meta$individual_id),
  deployments_tracks        = n_distinct(tracks$deployment_id),
  rows_tracks               = nrow(tracks)
)

count(st_drop_geometry(meta), manipulation_type)   # "relocated" should be gone
```
## STEP 1.4: Combine metadata and tracking data

We join the bird information to every GPS fix, matching on the deployment. `left_join()` keeps all rows of `tracks`.

```{r}
#| label: join
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)

# One row per deployment, with the names used in the rest of the template
birds <- meta %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(deployment_id,
         ID  = individual_id,
         dev = tag_id,
         age = animal_life_stage)

# Each deployment must appear only once, otherwise the join duplicates fixes
birds %>% count(deployment_id) %>% filter(n > 1)   # should be empty

data <- tracks %>% left_join(birds, by = "deployment_id")

nrow(tracks) == nrow(data)  # same number of rows as before: the join did not duplicate fixes

```
```{r}
write.csv(
  data,                # Your dataframe
  file = "C:/rug/github/FE2026/storks/data.csv",  # Replace with your desired path and filename
  row.names = FALSE    # Exclude row numbers in the CSV
)
```

# stop here
# PART 2: Cleaning tracking data

```{r}
#| label: filter-log
filter.log <- tibble(step = "raw data", n.fixes = nrow(data))

# Log of how many fixes remain after each filtering step
log_step <- function(log, step, df){
  add_row(log, step = step, n.fixes = nrow(df))
}
```

## STEP 2.1: Remove absent fixes


```{r}
#| label: filter-absent
data <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(long),
         !(lat == 0 & long == 0),
         between(lat, -90, 90), between(long, -180, 180))

# The data is an sf object: drop fixes whose geometry is empty
if (inherits(data, "sf")) data <- data[!st_is_empty(data), ]

filter.log <- logtree::log_step(filter.log, "absent coordinates", data)
filter.log
```
```{r}
#| label: join
birds <- meta %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(deployment_id,
         ID            = individual_id,
         dev           = tag_id,
         age           = animal_life_stage,
         session_start = deploy_on_timestamp,
         session_end   = deploy_off_timestamp)

data <- tracks %>%
  left_join(birds, by = "deployment_id") %>%
  mutate(dt = timestamp)   # the rest of the template uses dt
```
## STEP 2.2: Remove fixes outside the deployment

Tags often record positions before they are put on a bird and sometimes after the bird died or lost its tag. The deployment start and end in the metadata tell us which fixes belong to the bird.

```{r}
#| label: filter-deployment
# summary(birds$session_start)   # check for NAs first
data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter((!is.na(session_start) & dt < session_start) |
         (!is.na(session_end)   & dt > session_end)) %>%
  count(ID, name = "fixes.outside.deployment")

# Missing start or end dates are not treated as a reason to remove a fix
data <- data %>%
  filter(is.na(session_start) | dt >= session_start,
         is.na(session_end)   | dt <= session_end)

filter.log <- logtree::log_step(filter.log, "outside deployment", data)
```

## STEP 2.3: Remove outliers flagged in Movebank, and duplicates

Data owners can mark outliers in Movebank. We also remove duplicated fixes: rows of the same bird with the same timestamp. If a GPS and an Argos fix share a timestamp, the GPS fix (sensor 653) is kept.

```{r}
#| label: filter-outliers-duplicates
data %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  count(algorithm_marked_outlier, manually_marked_outlier)

data <- data %>%
  filter(!(algorithm_marked_outlier %in% TRUE),
         !(manually_marked_outlier  %in% TRUE))
filter.log <- logtree::log_step(filter.log, "marked as outlier in Movebank", data)

sum(duplicated(st_drop_geometry(data)[, c("ID", "dt")]))

data <- data %>%
  arrange(ID, dt, sensor_type_id) %>%
  distinct(ID, dt, .keep_all = TRUE)
filter.log <- log_step(filter.log, "duplicated timestamps", data)
```

## STEP 2.4: Remove poor-quality fixes

Our tags are Argos transmitters. Fixes from the GPS sensor have no quality fields here (`argos_lc` is `NA`) and are kept. Argos fixes get a location class: 3, 2, 1 and 0 have estimated errors from under 250 m to over 1500 m, A and B have no error estimate, and Z means the location is invalid.

```{r}
#| label: argos-quality
#| fig-height: 3
data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(lc = replace_na(as.character(argos_lc), "GPS (no class)")) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = lc)) +
  xlab("Argos location class") +
  theme_classic()

table(data$argos_lc, useNA = "ifany")
```

We remove the classes B and Z. Change `lc_keep` if you want to be stricter or more lenient.

```{r}
#| label: filter-quality
lc_keep <- c("3", "2", "1", "0", "A")

data <- data %>%
  filter(is.na(argos_lc) | as.character(argos_lc) %in% lc_keep)
filter.log <- log_step(filter.log, "Argos location class B or Z", data)
```

## STEP 2.5: Flag implausible altitudes

Altitude is much less precise than position, so rather than throwing away good positions because of a bad altitude, we set implausible altitudes to `NA`. Storks soar in thermals and cross high ground on migration, so I allow a wide range of -100 to 5000 m. `height_raw` (GPS) is stored as text, so it is converted to numbers first. It is a height above the ellipsoid, not above sea level, so it can differ from true altitude by a few tens of metres.

```{r}
#| label: filter-altitude
alt_min <- -100
alt_max <- 5000

summary(as.numeric(as.character(data$height_raw)))
summary(data$argos_altitude)

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    alt_gps   = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(height_raw))),
    alt_gps   = if_else(alt_gps < alt_min | alt_gps > alt_max, NA_real_, alt_gps),
    alt_argos = if_else(argos_altitude < alt_min | argos_altitude > alt_max,
                        NA_real_, argos_altitude)
  )

colSums(is.na(st_drop_geometry(data)[, c("alt_gps", "alt_argos")]))
```
